title: India Condemns 'Deeply Concerning' Attacks on Two Indian-Crewed Tankers in Gulf of Oman
excerpt: The MEA's Sunday statement confirmed MT Petro Dolphin's drone strike at Sohar Anchorage — nine of 11 Indian crew safe, two missing — and a projectile strike on MT Valthera, whose 11 Indian seafarers are safe, while urging de-escalation.
body:
• The Ministry of External Affairs on Sunday condemned attacks on two commercial vessels carrying Indian crews in the Gulf of Oman region, calling the repeated strikes "deeply concerning" and demanding an immediate end to attacks on commercial shipping.
  • The drone-struck tanker MT Petro Dolphin was hit at Sohar Anchorage on Saturday, October 11: nine of its 11 Indian seafarers have been rescued and are safe, while two remain missing as Omani coast guard search-and-rescue operations continue.
  • A second vessel, the Marshall Islands-flagged MT Valthera, was struck by an unknown projectile with a fire onboard — all 11 of its Indian seafarers are reported safe.

India on Sunday condemned the attacks on two commercial vessels carrying Indian seafarers in the Gulf of Oman region, calling the recurring strikes on merchant shipping "deeply concerning" and urging an immediate de-escalation and a diplomatic resolution of the US-Iran conflict.

The Ministry of External Affairs said the Nicaragua-flagged tanker MT Petro Dolphin was reportedly struck by a drone at Sohar Anchorage on Saturday, October 11, with two of the 11 Indian seafarers onboard still missing. "We condemn the attacks on commercial vessels in the Strait of Hormuz region on 11 October 2026," the ministry said in its statement. "The safety and security of Indian seafarers remain a priority for the government of India."

Two ships, 22 Indian seafarers

Union Minister for Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal confirmed the Petro Dolphin attack on social media, saying nine of the 11 Indian crew members had been successfully rescued and were safe. "Search-and-rescue operations are actively underway by the local Coast Guard. We are continuously coordinating with all relevant authorities to fully support the ongoing rescue efforts and ensure every possible action is taken to safely locate our missing personnel," Sonowal said on X.

https://x.com/pati_marins64/status/2109125063844733380

The MEA statement revealed a second incident the same day: the Marshall Islands-flagged tanker MT Valthera was struck by an unknown projectile, sparking a fire onboard. All 11 Indian seafarers on the Valthera are reported safe, according to the ministry.

The Embassy of India in Muscat said it was closely monitoring both situations. "The Embassy is in close and continuous contact with the concerned authorities," the mission said on X, and is coordinating with Omani authorities and the ship management companies on the rescue of the missing Indians and assistance to the rest of the crew.

"The targeting of commercial shipping, seafarers and civilian infrastructure in the region must end, and navigation and commerce through international waterways must be restored at the earliest."

— Ministry of External Affairs, India

A pattern of attacks on Indian-crewed shipping

The strikes are the latest in a string of attacks on vessels with Indian crews in the region. On October 6, the Panama-flagged tanker MT On Peace was struck by a projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz; of its 19 crew members, 17 were Indian nationals, and 12 crew — including 11 Indians — were injured. The injured were evacuated with the help of Omani authorities and treated in Khasab, Oman, after India condemned that attack too. Separate recent incidents off the UAE coast and the Black Sea have also left Indian seafarers caught in the line of fire, as The Videshi has reported earlier.

The Strait of Hormuz and the Gulf of Oman are among the busiest energy corridors in the world, and Indian-flagged and Indian-crewed vessels use them heavily for energy and trade. The recurring attacks have put seafarers — a profession in which India is one of the world's largest labour suppliers — directly in harm's way.

India's position: de-escalate through dialogue

The MEA reiterated the need for immediate de-escalation and a resolution of the ongoing conflict between the United States and Iran through dialogue and diplomacy. "The recurring attacks on commercial shipping in the region are deeply concerning and risk further aggravating an already volatile situation," the ministry said, calling on all sides to restore free navigation through international waterways at the earliest.

For Indian seafarers' families, the actionable point is vigilance and paperwork: keep the ship management company's emergency contact and the Indian mission's helpline in Muscat close at hand, and register travel with the embassy's community services before joining a Gulf-bound vessel. The two missing seafarers' families should expect the mission to coordinate directly with Omani search authorities — and the government has said the safety of the crew remains its priority.

What to watch

The immediate question is the fate of the two missing seafarers from the Petro Dolphin as the Omani coast guard's search continues. Beyond that, the coming weeks will show whether diplomatic channels can cool the Gulf flashpoint — or whether shipping insurers and crewing agents start rerouting around the region, with consequences for freight costs and for the thousands of Indian seafarers whose livelihoods run through it.
